Subject: Request: envelope encryption transit attestations + HSM role matrix

Hi Irene,

We're in the middle of a SIG risk review and the security team has asked for a couple of items around your envelope encryption and HSM operations so we can complete the control mappings:

- A per-region HSM operator/role matrix (who can wrap/unwrap, who can sign, separations of duties).
- A short diagram showing the envelope encryption flow for in-transit operations (where KEK/DEK wrapping occurs, which service performs unwrap, and network boundaries).
- Confirmation of whether any KEK wrapping uses customer-managed keys (BYOK) versus Redwood-managed KMS keys, and sample rotation cadence for KEKs.

We need these artifacts for our SIG CAIQ entry and to feed our procurement checklist. Timeline: would you be able to provide drafts by end-of-week (Fri 2026-10-08)? If not, an interim deliverable (role matrix + diagram) by Tue 2026-10-06 would be very helpful.

Thanks — let me know if you need a template or if we should escalate to procurement for an evidence exchange call.

Best,
Claire Huang
Senior Security Program Manager
BluePeak Analytics

Irene — attaching the first pass artifacts.

Attachments: hsm-role-matrix.xlsx (contains role, scope, allowed operations, region, justification), envelope-transit-diagrams.pdf (sequence diagram + service labels)

Notes / highlights from the matrix:
- HSM operators are scoped by region (us-east1, eu-west1). Only the on-call crypto-ops rotation and two designated engineering leads have KEK unwrap privileges; separation of duties enforced via RBAC + quarterly access reviews.
- KEKs are hardware-rooted: KEKs are generated/wrapped in our HSM cluster (Vendor HSM-Prime). DEKs are generated per-tenant in the service runtime and wrapped by KEK when written to storage.
- Next scheduled KEK rotation (policy-driven): 2027-01-15 for primary KEK; annual rotation cadence by default, emergency rotation procedures documented.

Laura: I left a comments tab for the diagram callouts where we should show the wrap/unwrap boundary and where TLS is enforced in transit.

-Jonas
Senior Systems Engineer, Crypto Infrastructure
Redwood Inference

Claire — attaching the artifacts Jonas prepared and a short signed commitment text. Per your checklist:

- HSM role matrix (attached) lists role-level privileges; PII was redacted. Operators are scoped by region; KEK unwrap limited to on-call crypto-ops and two engineering leads.
- Envelope transit diagram (attached) shows: client -> TLS -> ingress service -> DEK created -> DEK wrapped by KEK inside HSM cluster via secure channel -> wrapped DEK stored in object store. Unwrap occurs inside the same HSM boundary when decrypting for runtime.
- KEK management: Redwood supports both Redwood-managed KMS and customer BYOK. For BluePeak (tenant id: BP-998) the KEK is Redwood-managed; rotation cadence is annual with documented emergency rotation steps.

Links: Drive folder with source diagrams and export: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c
DocuSign for the signed commitment: https://app.docusign.com/containers/XYZ123

We've provided the files as requested. If you need explicit audit extracts (access logs for wrap/unwrap operations across a date range) we can pull those — let me know the date window and any redaction constraints and we can include them as a follow-up.

Regards,
Irene Choi
Director, Security & Compliance
Redwood Inference
